seo.title: New Zealand & Fiji Summer Program | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Four weeks in New Zealand and Fiji for 17–22 year olds: conservation with DOC, rafting in Rotorua, a Fijian village stay and coral restoration on Drawaqa Island.

hero.eyebrow: College summer program · New Zealand & Fiji
hero.headline: Four weeks of conservation, culture and island life
hero.intro: Work alongside DOC at Tawharanui, raft in Rotorua, stay in a Fijian village and help restore coral on Drawaqa Island, with free days built in to explore on your own terms.
hero.imageAlt: Students mountain biking on a trail through tall forest

items.title: Two countries in four weeks
items.body: Two weeks on New Zealand’s North Island, from the Bay of Islands to Rotorua, then two weeks in Fiji, from the Sigatoka Valley to Drawaqa Island in the Yasawas.

items.title: Conservation in both countries
items.body: Three days with DOC at Tawharanui in New Zealand, then sand dune, mangrove and coral conservation in Fiji. Real service you can talk about in applications and interviews.

items.title: A Fijian village stay
items.body: Three nights in Culanuku Village, starting with a welcome kava ceremony. We join our hosts for church on Sunday and head out on a fishing trip with the community.
items.imageAlt: Student on a boat holding up a string of fish

items.title: Free time built in, logistics handled
items.body: A free day at every stage, from Paihia to Drawaqa Island, to choose your own adventure. Three meals a day, lodging, in-country travel, activities, entry fees and guides are included.
items.imageAlt: Students mountain biking on a trail through tall forest

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Waitangi & Tawharanui
weeks.body:
Kia ora, welcome to New Zealand! You’ll meet your Program Instructors in Auckland and settle in at Ōrewa Beach for orientation. Then we head north to Paihia in the Bay of Islands, where we visit the Waitangi Treaty Grounds to learn how New Zealand’s founding document shaped the country. A free day lets you kayak, snorkel, dive, go sailing or take the ferry to historic Russell.

Then we drive south to Tawharanui Regional Park, set up camp and begin our conservation project alongside DOC.

weeks.title: Conservation & Rotorua
weeks.body:
We spend two more days on the conservation project at Tawharanui, then travel to Rotorua, the geothermal heart of the North Island. A free day lets you choose your own adventure: mountain biking, the luge, geothermal parks or the hot pools. Then we take on the rapids together on a white-water rafting trip.

We finish our time in New Zealand back in Auckland with a free day in the city. Head to the Viaduct, the museums or the Sky Tower, climb Mount Eden, or take the ferry out to Rangitoto Island.
weeks.imageAlt: Students mountain biking on a trail through tall forest

weeks.title: Village life in Fiji
weeks.location: Nadi → Sigatoka → Culanuku Village → Pacific Harbour, Fiji
weeks.body:
We fly from Auckland to Nadi and start our time in Fiji with an orientation. In the Sigatoka Valley we work on a sand dune conservation project at Sigatoka Sand Dunes National Park, then transfer to Culanuku Village, where a welcome kava ceremony opens our stay.

Sunday is a day for church and family, so we join our hosts for church, then head out on a fishing trip with the community. Next we move to Club Oceanus at Pacific Harbour and join a mangrove conservation project protecting the coastline.
weeks.imageAlt: Student on a boat holding up a string of fish

weeks.title: Drawaqa Island & farewell
weeks.location: Pacific Harbour → Drawaqa Island → Nadi, Fiji
weeks.body:
A free day at Pacific Harbour lets you go river tubing, visit Kila World or try the Beqa Lagoon shark dive. Then we travel to Drawaqa Island in the Yasawa group and stay at Barefoot Manta.

We spend a day on a coral conservation project, learning how reefs are restored, and have a free day to snorkel, dive, hike, kayak or swim with manta rays. We wrap up the program on the island, then head back to Nadi for our last night before flying home.

day.heading: What a typical day looks like

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: There’s a free day at every stage of the program: Paihia, Rotorua, Auckland, Pacific Harbour and Drawaqa Island. Pick an optional activity, explore with friends or just rest and catch up on laundry.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: Low activity level. Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors and new experiences will be fine. Expect rafting and snorkeling, optional kayaking, biking and diving, and some physical work on the conservation projects.

items.title: History and culture in two countries
items.body: Learn how New Zealand’s founding document was signed at the Waitangi Treaty Grounds, then live and learn alongside our hosts in Culanuku Village in Fiji.

items.title: Service you can put on your résumé
items.body: Hands-on conservation with DOC in New Zealand, then sand dune, mangrove and coral projects in Fiji. You’ll come home with real experience to talk about in college applications, job interviews and scholarship essays.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: This program has a low activity level and suits anyone of average fitness with an enthusiasm for the outdoors. You don’t need experience with any of the activities, but be ready to raft and snorkel, with optional kayaking, mountain biking and diving on free days. The conservation projects also involve some physical work.

items.q: How much free time is there?
items.a: This program is built for college-aged travelers, so there’s a free day at every stage: Paihia, Rotorua, Auckland, Pacific Harbour and Drawaqa Island. Instructors are always on call, and free time comes with check-ins and clear boundaries.
Mostly lodges and hostels, plus camping at Tawharanui during our conservation project, three nights in Culanuku Village in Fiji and Barefoot Manta on Drawaqa Island.

items.q: What is the village stay like?
items.a: We spend three nights in Culanuku Village. Our stay begins with a welcome kava ceremony, we join our hosts for church on Sunday, and we head out on a fishing trip with the community.
By group van in New Zealand, with a flight from Auckland to Nadi. In Fiji we travel by road transfer and by boat to and from Drawaqa Island.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
